verses.1: For the Chief Musician, on stringed instruments; a psalm of Asaph.
verses.2: My voice rises to God, I cry aloud, my voice rises to God, and He will listen.
verses.3: In my day of distress I sought the Lord; at night I lifted up my hands before Him, and my soul was not comforted.
verses.4: I remember God, and I am comforted; I meditate, and my spirit is revived. Selah.
verses.5: My enemies have surrounded me like a wall; I was troubled and could not speak.
verses.6: I considered the days of old, the years of eternity.
verses.7: I remember the melody of my song at night, I meditate with my heart, and my spirit searches.
verses.8: Will the Lord reject me forever? Will He no longer be willing to show favor?
verses.9: Has His steadfast love come to an end? Has He sealed it for generation after generation?
verses.10: Has He forgotten to be gracious? Has He withheld His mercy in His anger? Selah.
verses.11: And I said, “This is my sorrow, the change in the right hand of the Most High.”
verses.12: I will remember the deeds of the Lord, for I will remember Your wonders from of old.
verses.13: I will meditate on all Your works and speak of Your doings.
verses.14: God, in the holy one is Your way; who is like You, mighty God?
verses.15: You are the God who does wonders; who is great like You, O God? You have made Your power known to the peoples.
verses.16: You delivered Your people with Your arm, the children of Jacob and Joseph. Selah.
verses.17: The waters saw You, O God—the waters saw You and trembled, the deeps also were stirred.
verses.18: The clouds poured out their sound; the heavens gave forth their voice, yes, Your arrows flitted.
verses.19: The voice of Your thunder in the wheel, the lightnings lit up the earth; the land trembled and the world quaked.
verses.20: Your way was in the sea, Your path in the mighty waters, and Your footprints were not known.
verses.21: You led Your people like a flock, by the hand of Moses and Aaron.

notes:
Notes  
- v. 1: The heading “For the Chief Musician, on stringed instruments” is a standard musical instruction.  
- v. 4: “Selah” is retained as an unknown musical or liturgical marker.  
- v. 5: “My enemies have surrounded me like a wall” translates שְׁמֻרוֹת as a metaphor for encircling or surrounding.  
- v. 16: The name “Joseph” is used here as a proper name, referring to Jacob’s son.  
- v. 20: The phrase “Your footprints were not known” reflects the poetic emphasis on God’s inscrutable ways.
